summary: Intermittent 5xx spike on embeddings-upload route from mis-decompression at edge causing upstream runtime crash
description: Issue summary: Customers (primarily NovaSearch) report a sudden rise in 5xx responses on the /v1/embeddings/batch-upload endpoint beginning ~2026-03-12 09:40 UTC. Impact: ~8% error rate on that route for the customer fleet, elevated token reprocessing, and multiple failed client retries. Environment: Production (us-east-1) routed through the edge API gateway cluster E-03 to ephemeral serving runtimes. Observed behaviour: API Gateway logs show 'invalid compressed chunk' parse errors interleaved with upstream pool resets. Upstream runtime logs show repeated worker process SIGABRT and OOM-like exits around the same timestamps. Expected behaviour: normal successful 200 responses for multipart/gzip uploads. Initial hypothesis: a mismatch in compression handling between the client (NovaSearch SDK v1.4 which does chunked gzip) and an edge decompression optimization introduced in apigw (decompress-on-proxy for small chunks). This causes the gateway to mis-interpret chunk boundaries on specific multipart upload shapes, returning 5xx and forwarding malformed data to runtimes which subsequently crash while parsing the payload. Temporary workaround: support instructed NovaSearch to disable client-side gzip for uploads and re-run; early indicators show error rate falls back to baseline for that customer. Next steps: reproduce, patch apigw, and harden runtime parsing.
steps_to_reproduce: Use NovaSearch SDK v1.4 upload example: POST /v1/embeddings/batch-upload with Transfer-Encoding: chunked and Content-Encoding: gzip on a 40MB multipart payload composed of 12 parts
Send at ~40 concurrent streams from a single client IP with keepalive enabled
Observe apigw E-03 logs for 'invalid compressed chunk' and 5xx responses
Correlate with serving-runtime r-xx worker logs for process crashes and SIGABRT entries
logs: apigw/E-03 2026-03-12T09:41:02Z ERROR parse_compressed_chunk: invalid header at offset 1432 (trace_id=tx-8f7a)
runtime/r-21 2026-03-12T09:41:04Z WORKER 7 SIGABRT parsing request trace_id=tx-8f7a payload_size=41_203_114
runtime/r-21 2026-03-12T09:41:04Z OOM? meminfo: rss=3.2GB vms=11.1GB gpu_mem=6.7GB
comments: 2026-03-12 10:05 - Support (Aisha): Received report from NovaSearch; elevated 5xx on embeddings upload. Collected basic logs and asked for sample curl reproducer.

2026-03-12 10:18 - SRE (Tomás): Noticed apigw E-03 shows decompression parse errors coincident with runtime restarts. Rolling a temporary config to disable edge auto-decompress for uploads on E-03 only.
2026-03-12 10:22 - Customer (NovaSearch - Kate L.): Confirmed they can disable gzip client-side temporarily; will test and report back in 15m.
2026-03-12 10:40 - Customer (Kate L.): After disabling gzip, error rate dropped to <0.5% — seems to confirm compression path is contributing.

2026-03-12 11:05 - Dev (Jenna): Reproduced locally using the same payload shape; apigw decompressor emitted malformed frames when chunk boundary aligns with compressed block boundary. Filing PR to add stricter boundary checks.
2026-03-12 12:30 - SRE (Tomás): Deployed hotfix to apigw E-03 to disable streaming-decompress optimization and enabled payload size/liveness guard on runtime. Monitoring for 30m.
2026-03-12 13:05 - Support (Aisha): NovaSearch confirms normal traffic after mitigation. Marking incident as mitigated; keeping ticket open for root cause patch and postmortem.
investigation_notes: Edge decompressor optimization (PR #4156) introduced a fast-path that assumes chunk boundaries align with gzip block boundaries for payloads smaller than 512KB — violated by NovaSearch multipart style leading to mis-parse.
Correlation: 94% of apigw parse errors originated on a single edge cluster E-03 handling NovaSearch's regional ingress due to affinity routing.
Runtime crashes were triggered by attempts to process partially decompressed payloads: parser exceptions surfaced as SIGABRT in worker 7; stacktrace points at parse_gzip_stream()+0x2c1.
Memory footprints during incident were elevated but not outside expected headroom; primary failure mode is parsing exception not pure OOM in most reproductions.
Customer SDK pattern: chunked gzip + multipart leads to compressed block boundary splits that our decompressor fast-path didn't handle.
Related internal ticket: INT-3321 allocated to runtime parsing hardening.
Temporary mitigation confirmed effective: disabling apigw auto-decompress for upload route reduces 5xx and prevents runtime crash propagation.

Next actions: ship apigw fix with robust gzip streaming boundary checks, add e2e test covering chunked multipart compressed uploads, and harden runtime parser to fail-safe on malformed streams (fail earlier and return 4xx instead of crashing worker).
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied: disabled apigw streaming-decompress fast-path on affected edge clusters and recommended NovaSearch toggle off gzip on client while fix rolls out. Patch PRs opened for apigw and runtime. Long-term: add unit/e2e tests for gzip+chunked+multipart patterns, instrument decompressor to fail fast and return 4xx for malformed compressed streams instead of forwarding to runtime. Monitoring: increased logging and alert on decompressor-parse-errors threshold. Customer follow-up scheduled: 2026-03-15 16:00 UTC postmortem call.
